newsitem.title: USA: Fed did not get durables data early - U.S. Commerce.
newsitem.headline: Fed did not get durables data early - U.S. Commerce.

text.p: A U.S. Commerce Department official on Thursday said the Federal Reserve Board did not receive the August report on durable goods orders ahead of its release today at 8:30 a.m. (1230 GMT)

"There is no evidence that any premature release of data occurred surrounding the durable goods release Sept. 26, 1996," said Jane Callen, a Commerce official who conducts briefings where economic indicators are released.
She said the department adheres strictly to a directive that prohibits the early release of the data to anyone other than the President through the Council of Economic Advisers.
Executive branch officials who receive the data are prohibited from releasing the data or commenting on it ahead of the scheduled release time.
The Commerce Department's report of a 3.1 percent drop in August durable goods orders hinted at greater-than-expected weakness in the manufacturing sector.
That fuelled some talk that perhaps some members of the Federal Reserve policy-setting Open Market Committee had the data at the time of their most recent meeting on Sept. 24.
At that meeting, the Fed surprised many economists by refraining from raising interest rates. A number of economists felt a rate rise was necessary to cool down the economy.
